definitions: To scratch, scrape, or rub a surface to relieve an itch, remove an outer layer, or produce sound.
(Familier) To gain or scrape together small amounts of time, money, or advantages, often through petty calculation.

Usage note: Often intransitive in colloquial use to describe physical discomfort ("ça me gratte"), or used transitively in idiomatic phrases like "gratter du papier" (to write routinely or excessively).
examples: Le chien ne cesse de se gratter l'oreille depuis ce matin.
The dog has not stopped scratching its ear since this morning.
En négociant fermement chaque clause du contrat, il a réussi à gratter quelques jours supplémentaires.
By negotiating every clause of the contract firmly, he managed to scrape an extra few days.
Cette étiquette en nylon me gratte affreusement dans le cou.
This nylon tag is itching horribly against my neck.

examples: Le projet de loi a été adopté en séance plénière, nonobstant les réserves émises par le Conseil d'État.

definitions: Just, simply; modal particle expressing that a fact, situation, or consequence is unavoidable, self-evident, or must be accepted as it is (umgangssprachlich).

Usage note: Common in spoken German and informal prose, functioning similarly to "eben"; it cannot be stressed when used as a modal particle and typically does not occupy the first position in a main clause.
examples: Wenn der Zug Verspätung hat, müssen wir halt warten.
If the train is delayed, we simply have to wait.
Es ist zwar ärgerlich, aber jetzt ist es halt passiert.
It is annoying, but now it has just happened.
